explanation: Often called horned toads, these desert lizards raise blood pressure in the head until vessels near the eyes rupture. Coyotes and dogs find the blood foul-tasting.

claims.text: Several horned lizard species (Phrynosoma) can squirt blood from the eyes as a defence.
Frilled lizards, Gila monsters and green iguanas do not squirt blood from their eyes.
Horned lizards are often called horned toads.
Horned lizards squirt blood by raising blood pressure in the head until vessels around the eyes rupture.
The squirted blood deters dogs and coyotes, which find it distasteful.

evidence.restatement: Several Phrynosoma species squirt blood from the eyes when threatened.
Frilled lizards spread a neck frill, Gila monsters bite with venom and green iguanas lash their tails; none squirts blood from its eyes.
Horned lizards are widely nicknamed horned toads or horny toads.
They raise blood pressure in the head until small vessels around the eyelids rupture and squirt blood.
Dogs and coyotes find the blood distasteful, as experiments by Middendorf and Sherbrooke showed.
